newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P assigns A-minus to Amcor notes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P assigns A-minus to Amcor notes.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Wednesday it had assigned an A-minus long-term rating to Amcor Ltd's US$200 million convertible subordinated perpetual notes issue.
S&P said the outlook was stable.

It said the notes were direct, unsecured obligations of Amcor, subordinated to all senior debt of the company, and were convertible into Amcor ordinary shares at any time within 10 years of issue. The notes have no maturity and are redeemable only at the company's option after 10 years from issue.
The A-minus rating was notched from Amcor's A long-term corporate credit rating, the U.S. ratings agency said.

"Amcor's A corporate credit and A-1 short-term ratings reflect the company's solid business positions in diverse packaging and paper markets in Australasia, a growing offshore position in core products, a high level of operational integration in Australia, moderate cost position, and moderately conservative finances," S&P said.
